---

Ten FamilySearch searches were run looking for a man named Bartholomew Flynn who may have been a brother of Patrick Flynn. The searches covered both Ireland and the United States, tried his name with and without his parents' names (Thomas and Mary Flynn), tried the common Irish nickname "Bartley" for Bartholomew, and tried wildcard spellings to catch indexing variants. Every single search returned zero results — including a bare search on the surname Flynn alone, which in a fully live index would normally return thousands of records. This tells us the FamilySearch index is not surfacing any Flynn records in this environment at all, so the absence of Bartholomew cannot be treated as evidence he did not exist.

Next, the same search would need to be tried on external genealogy websites — such as Ancestry or Findmypast — which hold Irish Catholic parish registers and US census records that may not overlap with what FamilySearch indexes.
